propositions: Hand-rolled CLI argument parsing loops in claim.py and transition.py must be refactored to use Python's stdlib argparse framework while preserving all observable behavior including command-specific --force semantics and --assignee None-vs-empty-string sentinel.

Unknown/extra CLI tokens must be silently skipped via parse_known_args; --help remains dispatcher-served byte-exact from golden help files (not argparse-regenerated); prefix abbreviations must be disabled (allow_abbrev=False).

The --force parameter has command-specific semantics: claim bare --force consumes next non-option token as reason else defaults to "(no reason given)"; transition bare --force sets force_reason="" (None only when absent) and must NOT consume following tokens; both commands support --force=<reason> inline form.

The --assignee parameter must maintain its None-vs-empty-string distinction: absent argument → None (triggers default_assignee fallback), explicit --assignee "" → empty string (clears assignee), and value-less usage → exit code 1.

transition._parse_flags must be retained as a thin argparse-backed shim returning the identical 5-tuple (reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref) to preserve its three external direct callers in tests.

Retired --force-close flag must be rejected with exit code 1 and existing error message; argparse error conditions (value-less, invalid flags) must exit 1 with historical messages not argparse's default exit-2 plus usage.
